16.0.0.en: 1- "Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust."

16.0.1.en: 1- This psalm begins with prayer, as David asks God to preserve him from dangers and death, since David was often exposed to Saul's pursuit of him, in addition to his wars with enemies, and then his flight from his son Absalom.

16.0.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ, who speaks in the name of the Church, and asks the Father to preserve Him; because He trusted in Him (Heb 5:7; Jn 17).

16.0.3.en: 3- David's faith in God appears here in his trusting in Him, so he is not troubled whatever dangers surround him; he is confident that He is able to preserve him.

16.1.0.en: 2- "I said unto the Lord, Thou art my Lord: my good is nothing without thee."

16.1.1.en: 1- David feels that God alone is his righteousness and his Lord, and it is a prophecy about Christ, who speaks showing His humanity, saying "my Lord"; because Christ by His Incarnation took the form of a servant, so the word "my Lord" suits Him.

16.1.2.en: 2- David sees that God is the source of his good things, so he hopes for none other, and feels his sufficiency in Him, while the world with all its delights cannot satisfy him.

16.1.3.en: 3- In the Septuagint translation it says, "Thou hast no need of my goodness"; David's goodness is from God, and it is a declaration from David that he does not depend on his own goodness, or strength, or any resources he has, but depends on God alone, the source of all good and strength. And this shows David's humility.

16.1.4.en: 4- God is David's good, not only by His gifts, but God Himself in His love is David's good; he contemplates His Person and praises Him and rejoices in fellowship with Him.

16.2.0.en: 3- "But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight."

16.2.1.en: The excellent: that is, the virtuous, who are distinguished by virtues.

16.2.2.en: 1- David's love for holiness and virtue appears in his love for the saints, that is, those who sanctify their lives and hearts to God. And the excellent, who strive to acquire virtues, and by them is meant all believers who strive in the way of righteousness, that is, the people of God. So he is encouraged by their company and encourages them. David loves holiness and virtue, and therefore he is bound to those who love them, for he is the one who said, "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!" (Ps 133:1).

16.2.3.en: 2- If this verse is a prophecy about Christ, then Christ shows here that His delight, His desire and His joy are in His children who strive in the way of holiness.

16.2.4.en: 3- In the Septuagint translation, that is, the Agpeya, it says "his land", that is, the saints live in the land of God; it is a feeling of the children of God that their life depends on God and is in His protection and they live for Him, therefore God rejoices in them, for they rejoice in their life in God, and God rejoices in their trusting in Him. And the Septuagint translation says, "He hath wrought all his pleasure in them", that is, the saints gave their life to God and trusted in Him, so God fulfilled His will in them.

16.3.0.en: 4- "Their sorrows shall be multiplied that hasten after another god: their drink offerings of blood will I not offer, nor take up their names into my lips."

16.3.1.en: 1- David shows the corruption of the way of the wicked unbelievers, who worship gods other than God, and declares that their sorrows are many, meaning the bodily and spiritual troubles that befall them; because God has abandoned them. Perhaps, if they believe, they will repent and return to God.

16.3.2.en: 2- These wicked people are a symbol of everyone who today depends on the powers of the world, such as money, lusts, or positions, and does not trust in God, so psychological and spiritual troubles befall him, and even if at first he gains some material things, he cannot enjoy them because of his agitation.

16.3.3.en: 3- David clearly declares that he does not share with these wicked idol worshippers in any sacrifices and does not pour out their blood before the strange gods, that is, the children of God today are not attached to lusts and do not share with those who love them, but trust in God.

16.3.4.en: 4- And David also, to protect himself from evil, does not mention the names of these wicked people or their gods with his lips; so that his heart is not attached, or his thought confused, by evil.

16.3.5.en: 5- God declares through the tongue of David that He does not permit or bless idol worship and the pouring out of the blood of their sacrifices, and He rejects these wicked people and does not mention their names, that is, there is no place for them in heaven with Him.

16.3.6.en: 6- During Saul's pursuit of him, David was compelled to take refuge in the Philistine city of Gath and in the land of Moab (1 Sam 27:3; 22:3, 4) and lived for a time among them, in flight from Saul, but he did not share in their idol worship; so he justifies himself in this by his saying "I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood."

16.4.0.en: 5- "The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot."

16.4.1.en: 1- On the other hand David declares his faith in God and his looking to heaven, where his eternal inheritance is, and God is also his cup, that is, all that God allows him of sufferings or blessings. And if he has lost something of material things through Saul's pursuit of him, or others', God will compensate him for them and restore them to him; because He maintains his lot, that is, his inheritance is not only in this world, but in great blessings in heaven.

16.4.2.en: 2- If we take this verse as a prophecy about Christ, we find that Christ says to the Father that His inheritance is in Him, so He declares as man that His hope is not on earth, but in heaven.

16.4.3.en: And He accepts the cup of sufferings which the Father allows for Him, that is, death on the Cross, and rejoices in the accomplishment of the salvation of mankind.

16.4.4.en: And the Father will restore to Him His inheritance, since He "maintains my lot", that is, keeps for me my inheritance, and it means the salvation of the souls of men so that they believe in Christ, and He rejoices in their salvation. That is, the inheritance of Christ is His Church, which He acquired with His blood.

16.4.5.en: 3- We see that David does not rejoice in being king on earth, but rejoices that God is his portion and his lot.

16.4.6.en: If only you would focus on your love for Christ, for He is the most precious thing in existence, and when you are raised to heaven nothing will draw you except His beauty, and you will contemplate Him for ever; therefore take care today for prayer, praise and contemplation.

16.5.0.en: 6- "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

16.5.1.en: Lines: plural of line, and what is meant is the measuring line with which the areas of lands were measured in ancient times. Pleasant places: the good condition, which is taken from grace, and what is meant is fertile land.

16.5.2.en: 1- David speaks with confidence after trusting in God, declaring that God's gift to him on earth will be a good and goodly land, and he means that God will supply his needs and give him abundant material gifts.

16.5.3.en: 2- The better inheritance and the divine gift to David is his place in heaven, in the new earth, for it is better than everything on earth.

16.5.4.en: 3- David enjoys God here on earth, and He gives him spiritual gifts, which are peace of heart and joy; God's gifts to him are abundant and goodly.

16.5.5.en: 4- If David expresses in the tongue of every spiritual person that his inheritance is God Himself, and this is the greatest thing in existence, God also rejoices in possessing the heart of David and of every believer. These souls are the inheritance of God, to whom He gives countless gifts on earth and in heaven, and the inheritance of God are the saints, who have loved Him with all their hearts.

16.5.6.en: 5- He says "the lines are fallen unto me", that is, it is a divine choice and a free grace from God, and therefore it is a precious gift that fills the heart with joy.

16.5.7.en: 6- If we look at verses 1-6, we understand that whoever trusts in God and rejects the lusts of the world and strange gods, his portion is God, so he lives reassured on earth and in great enjoyment in eternity. And the opposite is true, for whoever chooses the pleasures of the world is deprived of fellowship with God and the Kingdom of Heaven.

16.6.0.en: 7- "I will bless the Lord, who hath given me counsel: my reins also instruct me in the night seasons."

16.6.1.en: 1- David felt the grace of God upon him in His guiding him all day to the truth, that he might walk uprightly, so he thanked God and blessed Him; because He counsels him and guides him.

16.6.2.en: It is the work of the Holy Spirit, who worked in the Old Testament partially, and in the New Testament continually in the heart of every believer in the Church.

16.6.3.en: 2- Thanksgiving, praise and blessing God establish a person in a strong relationship with God and pour out upon him more abundant blessings, so he hears the voice of God more clearly and He guides him in all his steps.

16.6.4.en: 3- David does not tire of prayer, for he prays all day and in the night too, and even sits to contemplate God's works with him all day, and then he hears the voice of God from his depths, which his reins symbolize. So he is attentive all day by way of thanksgiving, and likewise at night he reviews himself, and so also hears the voice of God, and in this he keeps away from sin by day and by night.

16.6.5.en: 4- The night is an opportunity in which David examines himself for his mistakes all day, and God guides him from within and warns him to repent of his sins, so that he used to weep and make his bed swim with his tears, as mentioned in (Ps 6).

16.6.6.en: 5- The night is a symbol of the darkness of sin, and during it God stirs the depths of man, which alert him to repentance and return to God.

16.6.7.en: 6- The work of the Holy Spirit appears in this verse; He counsels David and every believer who is submissive to God during the day, and at night His voice rises and the person hears it clearly in the form of strong warnings about the mistakes that occurred during the day, and makes him watchful all night, for he is under the protection of the Holy Spirit, and therefore lives uprightly.

16.6.8.en: 7- The work of the kidney in the body is to purify the blood of toxins; therefore David borrowed it to express the work of the Holy Spirit in the depths of man, to purify him from every sin and lead him to repentance.

16.7.0.en: 8- "I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved."

16.7.1.en: 1- David sees that his life is not without God's being before him; therefore he strove to remember that God is always before him, to lead him in all his steps.

16.7.2.en: 2- We understand from the word "I have set" the importance of man's will; he must strive to remind himself of the presence of God, and then God favors him with the sense of the divine presence. Thus Elijah also felt when he said, "As the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand" (1 Kgs 17:1), and likewise Joseph, who felt the presence of God, so he did not accept sin with Potiphar's wife (Gen 39:9). And therefore we say in the Divine Liturgy, "Guide us, O Lord, to Thy Kingdom", and in the Coptic original we find the meaning more exact, which is "Take a way before us into Thy Kingdom", that is, God is the constant leader of the believer in all the steps of his life, until He brings him to the Kingdom.

16.7.3.en: 3- Since David feels God's presence with him, supporting him, and says "at my right hand", that is, giving him all strength, naturally he is not moved, however much the world is troubled around him.

16.7.4.en: 4- God is before me, that is, my guide, and at my right hand, that is, my support; God is everything in my life and with me at all times, so I am not moved.

16.7.5.en: 5- This verse is also a prophecy about Christ, who completed His ministry on earth, setting the Father before Him and at His right hand, for He is in the Father and the Father in Him; therefore He was not moved by persecution of Him and endured all the sufferings of the Cross for our sake. The Father is at the right hand of the Son and the Son at the right hand of the Father (Mk 16:19); because the two are equal in essence.

16.8.0.en: 9- "Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope." (literally: my spirit rejoiced; my body also shall dwell in security)

16.8.1.en: 1- If God is always before David, then naturally he is in marvelous joy and peace continually.

16.8.2.en: 2- The heart is a symbol of the feelings and depths of man, so the joy of the heart is the true, steady joy. And the spirit of man clings to God who satisfies it and rejoices, and then David feels that his body is in a quietness free from all anxiety and agitation.

16.8.3.en: 3- David's body dwells in security, that is, settles in peace, and his spirit exults within him; because it enjoys the sight of God and fellowship with Him.

16.8.4.en: 4- David's body dwells in security, that is, lies in the grave in security; because it awaits Paradise and the Kingdom. And the Septuagint translation in the Agpeya is clearer, for it says "my flesh also shall dwell in hope", and what is meant is the hope of the Resurrection.

16.8.5.en: 5- If Christ is the speaker, that is, this is a prophecy about Christ, He feels that He has completed His striving and His endurance of sufferings on earth and His steadfastness in the Father who is before Him and at His right hand (v. 8). Now in this verse He rejoices, after dying on the Cross, that He has accomplished the redemption and the salvation of mankind, and His body lies united with His divinity, secure in the tomb in hope of His Resurrection on the third day, when His luminous body is united with His soul which is united with the divinity, and then He appears to His disciples.

16.9.0.en: 10- "For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption."

16.9.1.en: 1- With faith and steady hope David declares that God will not leave his soul in Hades (Sheol), but it is a temporary period after which he is transferred to Paradise, when Christ accomplishes the redemption on the Cross; for David sees the promises from afar and greets them (Heb 11:13).

16.9.2.en: 2- David, who fears God, believes that he will not see permanent corruption, that is, eternal torment.

16.9.3.en: 3- This verse is the clearest verse about Christ, whose soul will not remain in Hades, but He only went down to Hades and brought Adam and his children up to Paradise, after He had bound Satan by the Cross. And likewise the word "thine Holy One" means Christ, who was like man in everything except sin alone; His body will not see corruption in the tomb, but the divinity united with it keeps it until He rises on the third day.

16.9.4.en: 4- The love of God appears in this verse, who blesses those who fear Him and crowns them with glories in heaven. And God shows His love for the saints by keeping the bodies of some of them without corruption to this day, such as the body of St. Anba Pishoy.

16.9.5.en: 5- Peter used the words of this psalm in his sermon on the day of Pentecost, when three thousand souls believed and were baptized (Acts 2:25-31).

16.10.0.en: 11- "Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore."

16.10.1.en: 1- Since David is reassured of God's presence with him and that his end will be with God in eternal bliss, he thanks God who has made known to him and makes known to him the spiritual means that give him life with God, that is, prayer, contemplation and love for all.

16.10.2.en: 2- He also thanks God, who satisfies him so that he is not attached to the world or abases himself before it, so he is always filled with God, and this naturally gives him gladness and joy.

16.10.3.en: 3- David sees that as long as he depends on God who is at his right hand and leans on His strength, not on himself or the resources of the world, he continues to enjoy the bliss of fellowship with God on earth, and then the eternal bliss after this life.

16.10.4.en: 4- Christ, who rose and whose body did not see corruption, raises those who believe in Him to live with Him in a lofty life while they are on earth, and also gives them by His Ascension into heaven joy and bliss with Him for ever, which cannot be expressed and surpasses all human imagination.

16.10.5.en: 5- "Pleasures for evermore" means that God will continue in the Kingdom to give us from the abundance of His favors and satisfy us, for life in heaven is living, renewed and growing in a spiritual way that surpasses our minds; it is not boring at all, but there is a joy that surpasses all our imaginations.

16.10.6.en: Remind yourself that God is before you at all times, so that you may be reassured and rejoice and at the same time fear Him, so that you keep away from sin and grow every day in knowing Him, until you set out to glories unspeakable in heaven. God, the giver of righteousness and salvation. A prayer of David. "Hear the right, O Lord, attend unto my cry"... (v. 1). Introduction:

16.10.7.en: 1- Its writer: David the prophet, who was distinguished by many prayers, and this whole psalm is considered a prayer, therefore it is written in its title that it is a prayer of David. Although the characteristic of all the psalms is prayer, this psalm is filled with petitions and supplications from its beginning to its end.

16.10.9.en: a - When David was fleeing from the face of Saul.

16.10.10.en: b - When he fled from the face of Absalom.

16.10.11.en: 3- This psalm comes from the heart of one who is wronged, who believes in God, who is able to do him justice and save him, and then he comes out reassured, triumphant by the power of God.

16.10.12.en: 4- If the title of this psalm is "A prayer", there are four other psalms whose title is also "A prayer", which are 86, 90, 102, 142.

16.10.13.en: 5- This psalm applies completely to Christ during His passion, so it is considered among the Messianic psalms. And the psalms from (Pss 16-24) tell us about Christ the Savior, and the clearest of them is (Ps 22), the beginning of which Christ said on the Cross ("My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"), and this psalm and the one before it, that is, (Ps 16), are very similar, so that the Fathers call them the twins.

16.10.14.en: 6- This psalm is suitable for the Church to say in every affliction, and for every believer, when any trial passes over him.
